newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Van der Horst says position healthy.
newsitem.headline: Van der Horst says position healthy.

text.p: Van der Horst Ltd said on Monday its financial position continued to remain healthy with a strong balance sheet and good cash flows.

It also said in a statement it had been informed by three major shareholders -- Johannes Kotjo, Johnlin Yuwono and Bambang Trihatmodjo -- that a portion of their shares held independently by banks as collateral have had to be sold.
It did not specify the number sold.
But it added that group chairman Kotjo had reaffirmed his commitment to the group that he will give his best efforts to build up Van der Horst's business and ensure its profitability.
Van der Horst said in the statement it wished to address recent concerns and market rumours reported in the Singapore media.

On talk of a "possible lengthy suspension" of trading in its shares, it said there had been no application to the Stock Exchange of Singapore for a suspension and it "does not expect any reason for doing so in the foreseeable future".
As for rumours about the cancellation of existing projects, it said these were unfounded as no projects had been cancelled.
In response to claims that auditors had refused to sign off on the group's interim accounts, the company said there was no need for external auditors to sign off on the interim accounts.
Van der Horst on Monday reported that half year net profits plunged 84 percent to Singapore $4.1 million. Its share price has recently slipped to its lowest levels since 1993.
The shares closed at S$2.19 on Monday, down three cents.
